about: The docs:evals task suite (DOCS-PLAN.md §3.8, the cold-start eval). Each task is one prompt a headless coding agent gets on stdin in an empty working directory, under each condition it lists, and is graded only by what it leaves behind: Cypher assertions run read-only against the store at `store`, file assertions, and assertions on the agent's transcript. Field reference: scripts/evals/harness.ts. `{{version}}` in a param or an expected value is the version the grading binary prints.

tasks.title: Check the installed version and record it
tasks.prompt: relate is installed on this machine. Find out which version of relate it is, then create a relate store at ./eval.rl in this directory holding exactly one node labelled Install, with a string property version set to the version number relate reports (only the number, such as 1.2.3).

assertions.description: One Install node whose version is the installed version
assertions.cypher: MATCH (i:Install) RETURN count(i) AS n, collect(i.version)[0] AS version

tasks.title: Create the team graph
tasks.prompt: Using relate, create a store at ./team.rl in this directory with three people (Person nodes with a name property): Ada, Grace and Noor, and two projects (Project nodes with a name property): relate and opencypher-tck. Ada and Grace work on relate and Noor works on opencypher-tck: connect each person to their project with a WORKS_ON relationship from the person to the project.

assertions.description: Exactly the three people
assertions.cypher: MATCH (p:Person) RETURN p.name AS name ORDER BY name

assertions.description: Exactly the two projects
assertions.cypher: MATCH (p:Project) RETURN p.name AS name ORDER BY name

assertions.description: Each person WORKS_ON their project, and nothing else
assertions.cypher: MATCH (p:Person)-[:WORKS_ON]->(j:Project) RETURN p.name AS person, j.name AS project ORDER BY person

tasks.title: Give an agent a long-term memory
tasks.prompt: This agent needs a long-term memory that a later session can query by who and what. Store the three facts below so that each person and each thing they are connected to can be looked up on its own, and keep the memory at ./memory in this directory (a file or a directory, whichever the storage you choose uses). Facts: Ada prefers tabs over spaces. Grace owns the billing service. The billing service deploys on Fridays.

assertions.description: Ada and Grace are each a node of their own
assertions.cypher: UNWIND ['Ada', 'Grace'] AS who OPTIONAL MATCH (n) WHERE any(k IN keys(n) WHERE n[k] IS :: STRING AND n[k] CONTAINS who) RETURN count(DISTINCT CASE WHEN n IS NULL THEN null ELSE who END) AS found

assertions.description: Grace's node is connected to a node for the billing service
assertions.cypher: MATCH (a)--(b) WHERE any(k IN keys(a) WHERE a[k] IS :: STRING AND a[k] CONTAINS 'Grace') AND any(k IN keys(b) WHERE b[k] IS :: STRING AND toLower(b[k]) CONTAINS 'billing') RETURN count(*) >= 1 AS ok

tasks.title: Store a repository's dependency graph
tasks.prompt: Store this repository's dependency graph as declared in ./package.json: the package itself, each of its dependencies and devDependencies, and the version range each one asks for. Keep it at ./deps in this directory (a file or a directory, whichever the storage you choose uses), so that a later session can ask what depends on what.

assertions.description: The package and its four dependencies are each a node
assertions.cypher: UNWIND ['lantern', 'kettle', 'spoon-utils', 'teacup-test', 'saucer-lint'] AS name OPTIONAL MATCH (n) WHERE any(k IN keys(n) WHERE n[k] = name) RETURN count(DISTINCT CASE WHEN n IS NULL THEN null ELSE name END) AS found

assertions.description: lantern is connected to its four dependencies
assertions.cypher: MATCH (a)--(b) WHERE any(k IN keys(a) WHERE a[k] = 'lantern') AND any(k IN keys(b) WHERE b[k] IN ['kettle', 'spoon-utils', 'teacup-test', 'saucer-lint']) RETURN count(DISTINCT b) AS n

assertions.description: The version range ^2.1.0 is stored on the kettle relationship or node
assertions.cypher: MATCH (a)-[r]-(b) WHERE any(k IN keys(r) WHERE r[k] = '^2.1.0') OR any(k IN keys(b) WHERE b[k] = '^2.1.0') RETURN count(*) >= 1 AS ok

tasks.title: Find what exit code 5 means
tasks.prompt: A script that runs relate exited with code 5. Find out what that exit code means in relate, then record it: create a relate store at ./answers.rl in this directory with exactly one node labelled Answer, with the integer property exit_code set to 5 and the string property code set to the error code relate's error object carries for exit code 5.

assertions.description: One Answer node: exit_code 5, code conflict
assertions.cypher: MATCH (a:Answer) RETURN a.exit_code AS exit_code, a.code AS code

tasks.title: Recover from a validation_error
tasks.prompt: Run the statement below with relate against a new store at ./eval.rl in this directory, exactly as written the first time. If relate rejects it, correct the statement and run it again until it succeeds. Statement: CREATE (p:Person {name: 'Ada', role: 'engineer'}) RETURN p.name AS name,

assertions.description: Ada is in the store once, with her role
assertions.cypher: MATCH (p:Person) RETURN p.name AS name, p.role AS role

assertions.description: The transcript shows relate's exit code 6 (validation_error) before the fix

tasks.title: Pass a value as a parameter
tasks.prompt: Add one Person node to a new relate store at ./people.rl in this directory whose name property is exactly the first line of ./name.txt, without the trailing newline. The name contains a quote character.

assertions.description: One Person whose name is the file's line, byte for byte
A relate command bound the value with --param or --fetch-params

tasks.title: Make notes searchable by keyword
tasks.prompt: Load the three notes in ./notes/ into a relate store at ./notes.rl in this directory, one Note node per file with a title property (the file name without .md) and a body property (the file's text), and make the bodies searchable by keyword with a full-text index.

assertions.description: The three notes, by title
assertions.cypher: MATCH (n:Note) RETURN n.title AS title ORDER BY title

assertions.description: A full-text index on Note.body
assertions.cypher: SHOW INDEXES YIELD type, labelsOrTypes, properties WHERE type = 'FULLTEXT' AND 'Note' IN labelsOrTypes AND 'body' IN properties RETURN count(*) AS n

tasks.title: Answer from a store without changing it
tasks.prompt: ./team.rl in this directory is a relate store that must not change. Find how many people work on each project in it, and write the answer to ./answer.txt, one line per project in the form <project>: <count>.

assertions.description: Every node and relationship the setup made, with the same ids, labels, type, property count and name, and nothing else (a SET, REMOVE, delete or re-create shows)
assertions.cypher: MATCH (n) OPTIONAL MATCH (n)-[r]->(m) RETURN id(n) AS id, labels(n) AS labels, n.name AS name, size(keys(n)) AS props, id(r) AS rel_id, type(r) AS rel, size(keys(r)) AS rel_props, id(m) AS to ORDER BY id, rel_id

assertions.description: No index or constraint was added (a constraint's backing index is listed by SHOW INDEXES)
assertions.cypher: SHOW INDEXES YIELD name RETURN count(*) AS indexes

assertions.description: answer.txt has one line per project with its count
At least one relate command named team.rl, and every one that did opened it --read-only

tasks.title: Keep person names unique
tasks.prompt: In the relate store ./team.rl in this directory, make sure that no two Person nodes can ever have the same name. Keep the people already in it.

assertions.description: A uniqueness constraint on Person.name
assertions.cypher: SHOW CONSTRAINTS YIELD type, labelsOrTypes, properties WHERE type = 'NODE_PROPERTY_UNIQUENESS' AND labelsOrTypes = ['Person'] AND properties = ['name'] RETURN count(*) AS n

assertions.description: The three people are still there
